sentences.text: There are two rule books, and they’re mostly identical.
The International rules, usually called the COLREGS, govern the high seas and the waters connected to them.
They come from a 1972 treaty, while the Inland rules are American law, covering our harbors, bays, rivers and the Intracoastal Waterway.
Each set applies to every vessel on its waters, whatever flag she flies.
It’s called the COLREGS demarcation line, and it’s printed on your chart as a dashed magenta line, usually stretched across the mouth of a harbor or inlet.
In Florida, you cross it every time you head out an inlet.
Here’s some homework: find it on your local chart this week.
It makes all of this real.
